mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Status of the corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home jurisdiction's company registry (e.g., Companies House, Hong Kong Companies Registry, State of Delaware Division of Corporations)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of passport and residential address proof of each general partner and any non-resident limited partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or equivalent sworn officer in the partner's country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency / Register of Directors and beneficial owners for UBO piercing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate services provider / registered agent of the foreign entity

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source of wealth declaration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Partner's private bank with KYC approval

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all partners, ultimate beneficial owners, and authorized representatives against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, UK HM Treasury freeze, EU consolidated sanctions list, and Canadian domestic lists issued under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Freezing Assets of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act. Enhanced due diligence required for all non-resident limited partners, particularly where proposed payment rails include cryptocurrency (USDC, tokens), under FINTRAC's guidance on virtual currency. PEP status must be queried against a commercial global PEP database; enhancements are mandatory for PEPs, their close associates, and family members. A negative vetting result and a reasoned 'deemed not suspicious' memo must precede any registration filing.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – Entreprise Register (online platform: https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca/en/accueil/)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official name must be in French. A name may include a recognized modern language wording if it is the natural name of a registered trademark used internationally or if the French translation would be misleading. The legal element must be 'société en commandite' (e.g., 'S.E.C.') or 'limited partnership' or its French equivalent 'L.P.' when the name is used in English outside Quebec. All constitutive documents must be submitted in French or accompanied by a certified French translation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 30 days of a refusal notice, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request with the Registraire des entreprises, citing the statutory basis for the name and offering rebuttal evidence. The Registrar must issue a decision within 30 days. If the Registrar maintains the refusal, the applicant may institute a civil judicial review before the Superior Court of Quebec (Code of Civil Procedure, CQLR c. C-25.01) within 30 days of the Registrar's final administrative response, or file a fresh application under a new name at any time.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is not per se recognized for a Quebec limited partnership. The law requires a physical place accessible to the public and where books and records are kept. A non-residential address, such as a shared executive suite or serviced office, is accepted only if it provides physical presence (staffed premises with postal handling) and does not consist solely of a postal drop-box. For a data-pipeline and API business, tax authorities may scrutinize for 'foreign base' presence; thus a virtual address without local employees or commingled equipment will likely be rejected as the registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 40% within the first year if non-resident partners are majority owners; rising to 75% upon a trigger event (e.g., USDC/Stripe merchant registration, one-side remittance, or a FINTRAC suspicious transaction report).

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec (CQLR c CCQ-1991), arts. 2236–2247 (limited partnership) and art. 2240 (limited partner contributions); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, ss. 16, 21 and 39–47; Regulation respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, r. 9.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Québec Enterprise Registrar)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. Contributions of general partners may be in cash, property or services; limited partners' contributions are determined in the partnership agreement and the amount contributed by each limited partner must be disclosed in the declaration of registration. No escrow, blocked deposit or bank guarantee is required under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST RESOLUTIONS OF THE MANAGING GENERAL PARTNER (GOVERNING BODY) — RESOLVED: (1) that the capital contributions set forth in Schedule A are accepted as fully subscribed, without any statutory or escrow minimum, and are credited to the partners' capital accounts per the Limited Partnership Agreement; (2) that the registered office is established at [Registered Office Address], Montréal, Québec, Canada, and the Registraire des entreprises du Québec is named as the public service registry; (3) that the Managing General Partner is appointed and authorized to execute banking and payment-processor mandates, including USD and USDC accounts; (4) that [Name] is appointed Secretary and Privacy/Compliance Officer with authority to maintain the minute book, file regulatory returns, and administer the AML/KYC policy.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Partnership Agreement Drafting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Online name search and reservation portal (Portail des entreprises)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Run a priority name search in the REQ central register and reserve the proposed limited partnership name for up to 90 days. Simultaneously, execute the limited partnership agreement (acte de société) identifying all general and limited partners, contribution amounts, profit-sharing, governance powers, and the restricted management participation of limited partners. If the partnership contributes an immovable, the agreement must be in notarial form.
required_dossiers: Limited partnership agreement (private writing or notarial deed)
Identification documents and registry extracts for corporate partners
Declaration of contribution by each limited partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a new reservation or contest the REQ decision before the Tribunal administratif du Québec within the statutory review period; refile with an amended distinct name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Declaration of Registration (Déclaration d'immatriculation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — electronic filing service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the declaration of registration specifying the limited partnership name, Québec establishment address, general nature of business (ISIC 6201 / NAICS 518210 — data processing and API services), names and residences of all general and limited partners, capital contributed by each limited partner, and the management powers of the general partner. Sign electronically with verified identity, pay the CAD 64 filing fee, and obtain the Québec enterprise number (NEQ) and certificate of registration.
required_dossiers: Excerpt of the limited partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ issues a notice of intention to refuse, the applicant corrects or completes the declaration within the notice period; a refusal may be submitted for administrative review and thereafter appealed to the Tribunal administratif du Québec.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Activation of Federal and Provincial Tax Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration Online; Revenu Québec — enterprise portal linked to NEQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the issued NEQ, activate the federal Business Number (BN) and register for GST/HST where annual taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 or voluntarily. Register with Revenu Québec for QST, source deductions and any employer accounts. Confirm invoicing headers displaying the NEQ and tax numbers, and update the partnership's mailing and establishment addresses in both registries.
required_dossiers: Partnership agreement with tax allocation clause
Identification of the managing general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If account activation is delayed, request a retroactive effective date and file initial nil returns; discrepancies between CRA and Revenu Québec data are reconciled through the Registraire-CRA intergovernmental data exchange process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office Adoption and Officer Appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Managing General Partner and internal governance records (minute book)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Fix the partnership's registered office at the declared Québec establishment; appoint the Secretary and Compliance/Privacy Officer; adopt resolutions approving banking and payment-processor mandates (Stripe and USDC treasury accounts), the AML/KYC policy, and signature authorities; maintain the minute book, register of partners, and the capital account ledger.
required_dossiers: Governance resolutions of the managing general partner
Partners' register and capital account ledger
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Drafting defects are cured by a ratification resolution of the managing general partner; legal counsel issues a corrected governance minute and the registry filing is amended online.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Occupancy, Fire Safety and Occupational Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipality (e.g., Ville de Montréal permitting service), local fire prevention department, and CNESST (Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify that the office premises are zoned for professional and data-service use; obtain the municipal occupancy permit or certification. For leased premises, confirm the landlord's fire-safety and structural certificates comply with the Québec Construction and Safety Codes, and register the establishment with CNESST as an employer with a workplace health and safety program.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal permit is refused, adjust the business-use description, apply for a minor variance, or relocate; fire-safety deficiencies are cured by landlord remediation followed by re-inspection by the local fire prevention service.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — ISIC 6201 / NAICS 518210 (software, data processing and API services) is a non-licensed service activity; related oversight: Commission d'accès à l'information du Québec (CAI) for personal data practices.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory operational or manufacturing permit required; municipal occupancy permit and, only where interior alterations are made, a permit from the Régie du bâtiment du Québec (RBQ).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — office-based digital service operations are not listed in the Regulation respecting environmental impact assessment (CQLR c Q-2, r. 23); no EIA study, attestation or authorization is required for this activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process effluent or point-source air emissions due to office-only activity; municipal sewer discharge limits for sanitary wastewater apply; zero VOC/HAP process thresholds; electronic waste (servers, hardware) must be transferred to authorized Recyc-Québec registered recyclers; any standby generator must meet applicable local noise and combustion emission limits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certificate issued by the local fire prevention service after inspection of exits, smoke detection, and emergency lighting; structural floor-load verification for high-density server racks per the Québec Construction Code; workplace clearance through CNESST establishment registration, mandatory first-aid kit, and posted health and safety notices.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - Agence du revenu du Canada; principal portal for Business Registration Online / My Business Account (GST/HST, payroll and corporate income tax), and Revenu Québec - bureau des services aux entreprises / Mon dossier d'entreprise (Quebec QST and provincial partnership registration).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident or resident general partner must first obtain a federal Business Number (BN) via CRA Business Registration Online. The BN and related program accounts, including the GST/HST account, are issued electronically upon submission of prescribed partnership particulars (legal name, jurisdiction of formation, place of business, partners' identity and percentages). In parallel, the limited partnership must register with Revenu Québec to obtain a QST account and a Quebec establishment identifier using the 'Entreprise' online registration service or the prescribed ART-1/RBQ form. Foreign entities with no Canadian or Quebec establishment may use a representative for service of process and tax administration where required. The CRA BN and Revenu Québec QST number must be quoted on all invoices, customs documents and tax returns.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate a check-the-box entity classification system; a limited partnership is statutorily fiscally transparent for federal income tax and Quebec taxation. The partnership is not a taxpayer for income tax; each partner computes and reports its allocable share of Canadian-source income. Elections available include partnership fiscal period selection, allocation formula in the partnership agreement, capital cost allowance elections, material interest in a partnership elections, and the annual/quarterly GST/HST filing election. In Quebec, the association may elect to be a 'specified investment flow-through' or similar under Quebec rules where applicable, and jointly elect under section 273 of the Excise Tax Act for an 'elected combined fiscal period'. No hybrid mismatch election exists because Canada applies anti-hybrid rules (section 18.2/18.3 of the Income Tax Act and Quebec mirror provisions) that prevent deduction/inclusion mismatches.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) federally and QST (Quebec Sales Tax) provincially; the combined GST+HST/QST regime functions as a destination-based value added tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 - the 'small supplier' threshold under the Excise Tax Act. A taxable person providing worldwide taxable supplies of more than CAD 30,000 in the current calendar quarter or over the four preceding calendar quarters must register for GST/HST and QST; Quebec applies a materially parallel threshold for QST purposes. Once exceeded, registration is mandatory effective from the date the threshold is first exceeded. Non-resident digital suppliers are also subject to simplified GST/HST registration rules irrespective of the CAD 30,000 general threshold where the supply is made to Canadian consumers in the ordinary course of e-commerce.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No universal electronic invoicing or real-time fiscal clearance mandate exists at either the federal or Quebec level. Registrants must issue invoices containing mandatory information (e.g., 'GST/HST' registration number and, for QST, the QST identification number), and must retain source documents and electronic records in a prescribed manner. CRA requires electronic filing for registrants whose annual taxable supplies exceed prescribed thresholds using GST/HST NETFILE or GST/HST EDI protocols; Quebec mandates e-filing of QST returns through Revenu Québec's online portal. API-based submission is available for high-volume filers and tax professionals. There is no government-issued digital stamp, digital signature or pre-clearance of each invoice before issuance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of goods that are exported in accordance with the Excise Tax Act may be zero-rated when the supplier sells goods to a recipient outside Canada and the goods are delivered by the supplier or common carrier to a destination outside Canada within 60 days, or are otherwise exported as part of a commercial shipment. Supplies of services (including data pipeline API aggregation, scraping services and proxy gateway services) are eligible for zero-rating when performed for a non-resident recipient, supplied to an individual outside Canada, or supplied in respect of real or tangible personal property situated outside Canada, provided the service is not in connection with property intended for use in Canada and is not supplied while the non-resident is present in Canada. Data/commerce scraping API supplied by a Canadian limited partnership to foreign customers and not consumed in the Canadian marketplace is an offshore service and qualifies for 0% GST/HST. The supplier must retain contemporaneous business records demonstrating the non-resident identity of the recipient, the place of supply, the nature of the performance, and the remittance of foreign currency consideration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: A valid Customs Export Declaration through CBSA (Canada Border Services Agency) electronic system or the equivalent Canadian Customs Invoice and cargo control documentation
Original or verified copy of the Bill of Lading (ocean, air, rail or truck) showing the exporter as the shipper and the foreign destination
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement/foreign exchange transaction record evidencing receipt of the export consideration in foreign currency
Commercial invoice and signed contract or service order demonstrating the recipient is a non-resident and that the place of supply is outside Canada
Carrier proof-of-export package, including outbound manifest or waybill, delivery confirmation at the destination, and any certificate of foreign customs clearance where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess a zero-rated export claim beyond the normal four-year limitation period in cases of misrepresentation, neglect or fraud (8 years or longer if wilful default). A successful reversal is subject to recaptured GST/HST and QST, arrears interest, and penalties. The Excise Tax Act imposes monetary penalties for false statements or omissions in respect of net tax: generally not less than CAD 250 and up to 5% of the understated net tax for negligence or intentional error, with a 10% penalty for repeat violations or deliberate tax evasion. Criminal prosecution for fraudulent export zero-rating can lead to fines and imprisonment. Quebec law imposes parallel administrative penalties under the Tax Administration Act and may deny the input tax refund claim, de-register the exporter and impose civil liability on the general partner for the limited partnership's unpaid taxes.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada; foreign-exchange policy is administered within the federal legal framework, including the Department of Finance Canada, the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, the Special Economic Measures Act, and the United Nations Act. Canada has no general foreign-exchange administration requiring prior approval for ordinary commercial remittances.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is freely convertible for ordinary current-account and capital-account transactions. Canada generally imposes no exchange-control registration, capital repatriation approval, mandatory local-currency conversion, or profit-remittance withholding solely because funds cross the border. Remittances remain subject to bank sanctions screening, anti-money-laundering controls, tax reporting, transfer-pricing requirements, partnership allocation rules, and applicable withholding tax. Payments to non-residents may require Canadian income-tax withholding, commonly under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act, unless reduced or eliminated under an applicable treaty and supported by prescribed documentation. Related-party funding should be supported by a partnership agreement, contribution or loan instrument, transfer-pricing analysis, beneficial-ownership evidence, and a clear business purpose.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada has no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement, mandatory conversion ratio, or general deadline for converting export receipts into Canadian dollars. Export proceeds may be retained in Canadian dollars or foreign currency and may be received into Canadian or offshore accounts, subject to contractual banking requirements, sanctions controls, tax books and records, GST/HST treatment, and applicable customs and export-control obligations. Foreign-currency receipts should be recorded using an appropriate accounting exchange rate and reconciled to bank statements. If the business exports controlled goods, technology, personal information, or services subject to sanctions or sectoral controls, separate federal authorization or reporting may apply.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account; no statutory capital escrow account is generally required for a Quebec limited partnership
Operational Account; optional segregated capital or client-funds account only where contractually or operationally justified
Operational Account; capital escrow is generally a contractual banking product rather than a Quebec limited-partnership statutory requirement
Operational Account; separate foreign-currency accounts may be established for USD and other settlement currencies
Operational Account; suitable for Quebec-based treasury, CAD/USD collections, and commercial payment services

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Desjardins Trust and Investment Services Inc. and applicable Desjardins commercial banking entity
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account; product availability and eligibility must be confirmed for the limited-partnership structure and non-resident ownership profile

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for payment collection and treasury support; low as a substitute for a Canadian operating bank account. An offshore electronic-money institution or payment service provider may support CAD, USD, card, ACH, wire, or stablecoin-related flows only within the permissions of its home-country license and its correspondent or sponsor-bank arrangements. It does not automatically provide Canadian deposit-taking, Canadian payment-service-provider registration, Canadian trust protection, or authority to conduct regulated activities in Canada. A foreign PSP providing payment functions to end users in Canada may fall within the Bank of Canada Retail Payment Activities Act framework, while money-services-business obligations may apply under Canadian anti-money-laundering law depending on the services and operating model. Stripe onboarding is subject to Stripe's Canadian availability, merchant underwriting, beneficial-owner verification, prohibited-business rules, chargeback controls, and settlement-account requirements. USDC receipts should be handled through a regulated or appropriately registered provider, documented as customer receipts or treasury transactions, and reconciled to CAD accounting records. Stablecoin acceptance does not remove sanctions, AML, consumer-protection, tax, GST/HST, or source-of-funds obligations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical attendance of directors is not generally mandated by Canadian corporate or Quebec partnership law for opening a commercial bank account. Remote onboarding may be available after satisfactory electronic identity verification, document authentication, beneficial-ownership verification, and risk approval. Banks may nevertheless require an in-person meeting, notarized or certified documents, video identification, a Canadian-resident authorized signatory, a Canadian business address, or a visit to a branch where the structure includes non-resident partners, offshore control, higher-risk payment flows, cryptoasset exposure, proxy infrastructure, or complex ownership. The bank determines the final onboarding channel under its FINTRAC compliance program and internal risk policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete or inconsistent Quebec limited-partnership formation evidence, including missing partnership agreement, registration information, certificate or declaration details, or unclear general-partner authority
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified or bank-acceptable copies of Quebec registration records, limited-partnership agreement and amendments, general-partner authorization, signing-resolution or mandate, business-number evidence where available, registered-office details, organizational chart, and a concise legal memorandum explaining the LP's management and signing authority

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque ownership or control involving non-resident limited partners, nominee arrangements, trusts, layered holding companies, or inability to identify the natural persons exercising control
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete ownership and control chart to natural persons, passports and residential-address evidence for relevant individuals, corporate registry extracts, trust deed and trustee information where applicable, beneficial-ownership declaration, tax-residency information, politically exposed person and sanctions attestations, and written explanation of each ownership layer

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear distinction between the limited partners, the general partner, the operating business, and any affiliated service or technology company
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed intercompany agreements, service and licensing agreements, contribution or loan documents, transfer-pricing policy, funds-flow diagram, invoices or sample contracts, management and control description, and board or partner approvals demonstrating arm's-length commercial purpose

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business described as web scraping, proxy services, data brokerage, or API access without clear evidence that collection and processing are lawful
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed acceptable-use policy, data-source inventory, website terms and robots-policy review, privacy and data-governance policy, Canadian privacy-law assessment, customer due-diligence policy, prohibited-use schedule, IP and contract-rights analysis, incident-response plan, and sample customer agreements excluding credential theft, circumvention, malware, fraud, or unauthorized access

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Proxy API, automated traffic, high-volume requests, credential-related services, or infrastructure characteristics suggesting cyber abuse, evasion, scraping of restricted data, or sanctions circumvention
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Technical architecture and traffic-controls memorandum, customer screening and KYB procedures, rate-limiting and abuse-monitoring controls, IP-blocking process, sanctions and export-control screening workflow, abuse escalation records, customer acceptance criteria, and independent cybersecurity or compliance assessment where available

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cryptocurrency or USDC activity that is not reconciled to identifiable customers, invoices, wallets, counterparties, or fiat settlement accounts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written virtual-asset policy, regulated-provider agreements, wallet-address screening methodology, blockchain analytics reports, transaction ledger, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth records, customer identification files, conversion and settlement records, sanctions screening, accounting treatment, and confirmation that customer assets are not commingled with operating funds

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected international payment volume materially exceeding the projected revenue, staffing, customer base, or operating footprint
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve-month cash-flow forecast, pipeline and executed customer contracts, pricing model, expected countries and currencies, transaction-volume matrix, payment-purpose taxonomy, staffing and infrastructure budget, and documented explanation for seasonal or launch-related spikes

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of personal accounts, third-party settlement accounts, virtual offices, payment intermediaries, or unrelated counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Account-opening policy requiring accounts in the LP or properly documented affiliate name, authorized payment-flow map, third-party-payment rationale, counterparty contracts, beneficial-owner verification, prohibition of personal-account use, and reconciliation controls

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media, sanctions exposure, politically exposed persons, criminal allegations, or high-risk-country connections involving partners, directors, customers, vendors, or beneficial owners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current sanctions and PEP screening results, enhanced due-diligence memorandum, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence, adverse-media response, legal opinions or court dispositions where relevant, country-risk rationale, and senior-management approval for residual risk

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Failure to explain Canadian tax residence, foreign-partner tax status, withholding obligations, GST/HST registration, or partnership allocation mechanics
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CRA business-number and program-account records where applicable, GST/HST analysis, partnership tax memorandum, partner tax-residency certificates, treaty-relief forms, withholding procedures, transfer-pricing documentation, annual tax-compliance calendar, and accountant confirmation of books and records

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route partner contributions or shareholder-affiliate funding directly from an account held in the documented contributor's name to the Quebec LP's Canadian bank account, using a clear payment narrative such as limited-partnership capital contribution, partner advance, or intercompany loan. Maintain the executed contribution or loan agreement, partner approval, beneficial-owner and source-of-funds evidence, bank advice, foreign-exchange confirmation, and accounting entry. Use the LP's legal name and Canadian account details consistently; avoid unexplained third-party funding. For CAD payments, use Canadian EFT or other bank-supported domestic rails. For USD or other currencies, use SWIFT cross-border wire instructions and, where available, a Canadian USD account to reduce unnecessary conversion. Confirm whether the contributing entity is a non-resident and assess Canadian withholding, transfer-pricing, thin-capitalization, interest, imputed-income, and partnership allocation consequences before funding. No general Bank of Canada pre-clearance or foreign-exchange approval is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use Canadian EFT or wire payments for ordinary vendor and contractor settlements, and SWIFT cross-border wires using accurate beneficiary, intermediary-bank, invoice, and payment-purpose information. SWIFT MT103 is a legacy payment-message description; banks may process the same payment through ISO 20022 formats such as pacs.008. Use commercial documentary letters of credit, standby letters of credit, documentary collections, or open-account settlement according to counterparty risk. A commercial LC should specify issuing and confirming banks, UCP 600 or other governing rules, presentation documents, shipment or service evidence, sanctions clauses, discrepancy procedures, currency, and fees. For software, data, cloud, proxy, and API services, retain contracts, invoices, delivery or usage evidence, export-control analysis, tax forms, and sanctions screening. Banks may reject payments involving restricted jurisdictions, prohibited cyber activity, anonymization intended to evade controls, or insufficiently identified beneficiaries. Reconcile each payment to the subledger, invoice, purchase approval, and bank statement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD forward contracts with an authorized Canadian bank or appropriately regulated dealer, supported by documented forecast exposures, approved limits, confirmations, ISDA or equivalent master documentation where required, and hedge-accounting or treasury records

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies or jurisdictions where physical delivery is restricted or impractical, subject to dealer eligibility, applicable derivatives rules, counterparty due diligence, collateral terms, and documented underlying exposure

Currency swaps or cross-currency swaps for longer-term funding or recurring currency mismatches, subject to dealer onboarding, netting and collateral documentation, liquidity stress testing, and accounting treatment

Foreign-exchange options, collars, and participating forwards may be available for genuine commercial exposures, but require enhanced suitability, valuation, premium, scenario, and break-cost controls

Spot foreign-exchange conversions through the operating bank or regulated payment provider for settlement and working-capital needs; avoid speculative trading, unapproved leveraged products, and transactions lacking an identifiable commercial exposure

stage_5.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Rules regarding annual confirmation for shareholding transfers
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% at the limited partnership entity (pass-through); partner-level combined federal/Quebec rates reach 53.31% for individuals and 26.5% for the corporate general partner in 2025.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No LP-level income-tax holiday. Partner-level incentives include the federal SR&ED investment tax credit, the Quebec development of E-business/technology credit, and the Canadian-controlled private corporation small-business deduction (when a corporate general partner is allocated income). Such benefits are claimable only by the taxable partner, not by the pass-through LP; abuse of an LP solely to monetize these credits is itself a fatal red flag.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA): T5013 Partnership Financial Return and T5013 Summary/Information Slips, filed electronically through CRA My Business Account, EFIL or XML/EDI. Revenu Québec: TP-600 Partnership Information Return and TP-600.D distribution schedules via ClicSÉEQUR Affaires.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; partner-level Canadian income taxes are generally paid by quarterly instalments, but the T5013/TP-600 information return is filed once per partnership fiscal period.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The T5013 and TP-600 must be filed no later than the last day of the fifth month after the partnership's fiscal period end (e.g., a December 31 fiscal period is due May 31 of the following year). If the LP's fiscal period ends other than December 31, the deadline adjusts to the fifth month after that fiscal period end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter total gross revenues from commercial web scraping, API gateway subscriptions, and metered usage fees before deducting expenses. Exclude GST/QST and any amounts received as a non-resident's passive rental amounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Convert foreign-currency receipts (USD, USDC) to CAD using the Bank of Canada noon exchange rate on the day of receipt or the period-end rate if using the periodic-average method. Report only Canadian-source business income; keep all Stripe payout and crypto-exchange statements as source records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim allowable operating expenses: cloud hosting, data-proxy network costs, API gateway licensing, subcontractor fees, bandwidth, chargebacks, legal and accounting fees, and Quebec provincial insurance contributions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses paid for services rendered by non-resident partners or affiliates must be supported by contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation and T106 reporting if above the C$1,000,000 threshold. Amounts constituting rent, royalty, interest, or management fees paid to a non-resident must be identified for Part XIII withholding assessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income or loss for the partnership fiscal period before allocation to partners. This is the figure carried to each partner's T5013 slip.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners are taxable in Canada on their share of Canadian-source business income. A non-resident limited partner with no Canadian residence is nevertheless required to report this amount on a Canadian T1 (individual) or T2 (corporation) return unless a treaty relief, waiver, or NR6/NR5 application changes the withholding mechanics.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation to each limited partner according to the limited partnership agreement's agreed profit-sharing ratio. Losses are subject to the at-risk rules for limited partners, and negative adjusted cost base cannot be applied unless repaid or immediately indemnified.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident limited partner, issue the T5013 slip and, where the allocation consists of interest, dividends, royalties, or rent, apply Part XIII withholding at the statutory rate unless a valid treaty claim (Form NR301/TRC) reduces it. Active business income is not subject to distribution withholding but remains self-assessed by the non-resident partner.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of T5013 or TP-600 attracts CRA and Revenu Québec daily late-filing penalties (C$100 initial + C$25 per day, capped to C$500 per return under ordinary circumstances but higher for repeated or gross negligence), over which interest (s. 161) is compounded daily. A partnership that fails to file may also lose the right to deduct losses or dispute an assessment; Revenu Québec adds 5% late-filing penalty and 1% per month (max 17%) on any unpaid balance assessed, and CRA may impose a gross-negligence penalty of 50% of the amount of tax evaded for knowingly omitting income.
